title: Seismic waves through the Earth
description: Pick an epicentre and watch P- and S-waves travel through a cross-section of the Earth. See where S-waves stop and where the shadow zones form.
simplifications: Waves are traced through a simplified, spherically symmetric version of the PREM Earth model (speeds accurate to a few percent). Real Earth varies from place to place.
Only direct, transmitted rays are shown. Reflections, P↔S conversions, surface waves and diffracted waves are left out.
The crust (about 6–70 km thick) is far too thin to see at this scale, and the source is 33 km deep.
Time is sped up: at 1×, about 30 seconds of Earth time pass per real second.
The shadow-zone limits come from ray theory (P ≈ 98°–145° in this model). Weak diffracted P waves reach out to about 104°, which is why textbooks quote 104°–140°.
